Wilted · Mac daily-driver walkthrough · 31 August 2026 · candidate evidence

Mac daily-driver review.
Signed content-viewport evidence.

This report is a screen-by-screen review of the Wilted Mac app as built from the candidate commit below. Every image is an app-owned, window-scoped capture of the Wilted process itself, taken during a signed local XCUITest session. It is candidate evidence for owner review. It is not owner acceptance, not a release record, and not evidence of any production, device, or store state.

It supersedes the 30 August report, which predates the podcast Feeds card in Larder. Every frame here was retaken; none is carried over.

2. Method and evidence labels

Pixels come from XCUIElement.screenshot() scoped to the Wilted app's own window. Nothing in this session captured the screen, the desktop, or another application's window. XCTest's automatic whole-screen recording is disabled at the project level — the generated scheme carries systemAttachmentLifetime = "keepNever", so no full-screen recording was written to disk.

Evidence typeRequired proofLimit
Exact processFresh signed app bundle built and signed by the same gate that runs the suite, launched per scenario.Does not establish release status.
Accessibility treemacOS Accessibility hierarchy queried live during the session by stable identifier, including route and control identifiers.Interaction inventory, not pixels.
Content viewportXCUIElement.screenshot() on the app's own window element — the geometry scope an AppKit reader would call NSApp.mainWindow.contentView — paired with a sidecar recording the window frame, the captured pixel size, the embedded pixel size, and the inset actually applied. Captured pixels equal the window frame, which is what makes a window-scoped screenshot a content viewport screenshot.The sidecar is written by the test process from the window element's frame, not from inside the app. It proves the capture covered the whole window; it does not independently attest the app's own view bounds.
Source inventoryShipping-view controls and system handoff descriptions.Not runtime or visual evidence.

Resolution and crop

Every embedded PNG is 1084x784 because a uniform 8pt inset per edge is removed from a 1100x800 capture: the window's rounded corners are partly transparent, and an uncropped frame can contain readable fragments of whatever sits behind it. The window was restored on a 1x display, so backing-scale is 1.0 and these frames are not Retina-native. They cover more of the interface than the 30 August set did — the window is 1100x800 rather than 900x450, which is why several items previously recorded as below the fold are now in the pixels — but they are softer. Text legibility, not layout, is what this costs.

3. Onboarding and first run

Wilted has no account creation, sign-in, or welcome sequence. First run opens directly on Larder with the composer and an empty saved list; the app is usable without configuring anything. Sync is opt-in and lives in Settings; it is not part of first run and does not gate any Larder function.

Subscribing to a podcast is likewise not an onboarding step. The Feeds card is empty until the listener subscribes, and it says so in place rather than hiding.

No separate onboarding screen exists in this build, so none is captured. If one is added, this report must be refreshed.

4. Larder

Larder is the primary library destination and the default route at launch. The sidebar (wilted-mac-sidebar) holds the wordmark and the three destinations: wilted-navigation-library, wilted-navigation-processor, and wilted-navigation-settings. The detail pane is wilted-mac-library-detail.

4a. Podcast feeds

The Feeds card is where subscriptions are seen and managed. Before it existed a subscription could be created and never inspected, silenced, or dropped.

  • Policy line (wilted-podcast-feeds-policy): “Feeds refresh when you choose Refresh. No feed downloads audio on its own; use Download on an episode to keep it offline.” There is no schedule and no automatic download, and the card states that rather than leaving an absent schedule to read as a hidden one.
  • Withheld count (wilted-podcast-feeds-withheld): shown only when a refresh held episodes back. Subscribing reaches back thirty days and later refreshes admit only what published after the subscription, so a long back catalogue does not empty into Larder; the count makes what stayed behind visible instead of silently missing.
  • Empty state (wilted-podcast-feeds-empty): replaces the rows when nothing is subscribed.
  • Per feed: a row wilted-podcast-feed-row-<id> with the show title, the feed host, a count line wilted-podcast-feed-count-<id>, a switch wilted-podcast-feed-enabled-<id>, and wilted-podcast-feed-unsubscribe-<id>.

Per-item controls carry a stable content hash in their identifier: wilted-article-row-item-<hash> and wilted-episode-row-item-<hash> for the rows, with wilted-article-actions-item-<hash> and wilted-episode-actions-item-<hash> for their action menus.

5. Always-visible bottom rail

The retained product direction is an always-visible bottom rail. Bottom is the accepted placement. The rail is present in idle and in playback, on every destination, and there is no separate Now Playing tab. Playback adds current-item state plus inline Transcript and Up Next expansion within the same rail.

Keyboard transports are exposed as wilted-player-keyboard-transports, and audio route recovery as wilted-player-route-recovery. Both are in the Accessibility tree for the playback routes.

6. Prep

Prep is a primary destination reached from wilted-navigation-processor; its detail pane is wilted-mac-processor-detail.

7. Settings

Settings is a primary destination reached from wilted-navigation-settings; its pane is wilted-mac-settings. It holds the sync surface (wilted-sync-controls) with wilted-sync-status, wilted-sync-detail, wilted-sync-producer-identity, wilted-sync-last-fetch, wilted-sync-last-send, and the refresh and upload controls.

8. Download and recovery states

Two failure states are captured from fixtures that force the failure rather than describing it. Each shows the point at which recovery is offered.

9. Roles and permission differences

Wilted Mac has no user roles, no sign-in, and no per-user authorization surface, so there is no role-dependent route or control to show. The only permission-shaped variation is iCloud account availability, which changes the Settings sync surface and is captured in frame 8.2. The app requests no microphone, camera, location, or Screen Recording permission, and this capture session triggered no system permission prompt.

10. System-owned boundaries

Finder is the inventoried system-owned handoff for a retained recovery copy. No Finder window was entered during this session, and no Finder, permission prompt, account picker, browser, or desktop surface appears in any embedded frame — by construction, since every frame is scoped to the Wilted window and the 8pt inset removes the transparent corner region where background pixels could otherwise show. No system-owned sheet was opened or captured.

11. Coverage limits

These are the parts of the walkthrough this evidence does not cover. They are listed rather than omitted.

  • Not Retina. The window was restored on a 1x display, so every frame is 1:1 rather than 2x. Layout and control inventory are readable; fine text is soft.
  • Fixture audio does not play. The playing fixture points at no real media, so the rail reports “Playback is unavailable.” and the transport sits at 0:00 of 2:00. Frames 5.1–7.1 therefore evidence the rail's presence, inventory, and persistence across routes, not that audio decoded. The message appearing twice is a real observation about fault reporting stacking rather than replacing; it is recorded as a defect, not presented as intended behaviour.
  • Unsubscribe is not pixel-evidenced. The smoke suite drives it and asserts the row is removed. No frame here shows before and after.
  • Transcript content. Frame 5.2 shows the expanded panel with no transcript text, because the fixture has none.
  • Active preparation progress. No fixture sets an in-flight preparation, so Prep progress and cancellation cannot be reached from a test and are not pixel-evidenced. Frame 6.1 shows Prep without an active run.
  • Startup recovery. The startup recovery screen requires the local library store to fail to open. No fixture forces that, so it is not reachable from a capture test and is not evidenced.
  • Not exercised in pixels. Offline-cached state, item removal, search, relaunch continuity, a successful retry, and the Feeds empty state are described by control inventory only. No frame here asserts any of them.

12. Non-claims

Production CloudKit is not claimed. physical-device is not claimed. App Store Connect is not claimed. TestFlight is not claimed. deployment is not claimed. publication is not claimed. owner acceptance remains pending. This report is candidate evidence produced from a local signed build; it establishes what the app rendered on this machine at this commit and nothing beyond that.

13. Owner acceptance checklist

  1. Review the Podcast feeds card: policy wording, per-feed switch, unsubscribe, and count lines (frames 4.1, 4.2).
  2. Review Larder, Prep, and Settings with the always-visible bottom rail present in idle and in playback (frames 4.1, 5.1, 6.1, 7.1).
  3. Review the transport inventory and the inline Transcript and Up Next expansion (frames 5.1–5.3).
  4. Review the download failure and sync quarantine states and the recovery each offers (frames 8.1, 8.2).
  5. Read section 11 and decide whether any uncovered state must be captured before acceptance.
  6. Accept the Mac app for daily use, or return specific feedback. Owner acceptance is a human-only gate and no part of this report substitutes for it.
